title: A Review of AI Tools: Definitions, Functions, and Applications for K-12 Education
venue: AI, Computer Science and Robotics Technology
extended_summary:
This paper reviews artificial intelligence tools and platforms relevant to K-12 education, with the goal of giving teachers a practical reference for understanding what AI tools exist, how they are used, and what risks accompany their use. Rather than testing a single intervention, the article synthesizes definitions, functions, and categories of AI in education and then surveys a set of currently popular tools. The review is especially concerned with classroom uses such as instructional support, lesson planning, assessment, tutoring, and predictive analytics.

The paper discusses AI applications including machine learning, intelligent tutoring systems, automated essay scoring, natural language processing, chatbots, adaptive learning systems, and early warning systems. It also classifies tools into instructional, administrative, and analytical categories, and provides examples such as ChatGPT, Chat for Schools, Class Companion, Copilot, Diffit, DreamBox, Eduaide.AI, Khanmigo, MagicSchool, PowerBuddy, and SchoolAI. These tools are framed as supports for teachers, students, parents, and school systems in K-12 settings, including uses for lesson planning, feedback, differentiated instruction, and monitoring student progress.

The main conclusions are that AI can enhance teaching and learning, support personalization, reduce administrative burden, and help identify student needs, but it also raises important concerns about privacy, bias, misinformation, surveillance, and overreliance on automation. The authors emphasize that teachers and administrators should choose tools carefully, align them with curriculum and student needs, and consider ethical safeguards such as data protection, transparency, and human oversight. The article is positioned as a reference and guidance document for educators and future researchers rather than an empirical study of implementation in schools.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative AI / chatbot systems used for drafting, tutoring, summarizing, feedback, and other language-based educational tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: This paper is a review of AI tools for K-12 education; it discusses generative AI tools such as ChatGPT and other generative AI applications as examples of tools students and teachers can use, but does not evaluate a single generic system empirically.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot for text generation, summarization, drafting, brainstorming, and conversational assistance.
identified_tools.use_case: Discussed as a popular AI tool in K-12 education and as an example of a generative AI application students may use as a personal tutor; the review also notes school-district restrictions and privacy options.

identified_tools.name: Khanmigo
identified_tools.description: Khan Academy's AI-powered teaching assistant and tutor that provides instructional support, lesson-planning materials, and conversational help.
identified_tools.use_case: Reviewed as an AI-powered tool for learning and teaching, including standards-aligned lesson plans, rubrics, exit tickets, writing coaching, and tutoring.

identified_tools.name: MagicSchool
identified_tools.description: An AI platform for teachers and students that supports lesson planning, feedback, assessments, communication, and instructional coaching features.
identified_tools.use_case: Reviewed as a leading AI platform for schools, including its teacher tools and the Raina instructional coach chatbot, plus a student version under teacher supervision.

identified_tools.name: SchoolAI
identified_tools.description: An all-in-one AI platform for K-12 classrooms that can generate instructional materials, adapt text, support tutoring, and provide teacher monitoring and control.
identified_tools.use_case: Reviewed as a classroom AI platform used to generate lesson plans, automate assessment, personalize tutoring, and provide data-driven insights with monitored student spaces.

identified_tools.name: Class Companion
identified_tools.description: An AI-generated feedback tool for written assignments that provides instant, personalized feedback and reporting for teachers.
identified_tools.use_case: Reviewed as a writing-feedback platform that gives students immediate feedback and allows teachers to track progress and use rubrics.

identified_tools.name: Diffit
identified_tools.description: An AI platform for teachers that adapts and differentiates instructional content based on existing curriculum or source materials.
identified_tools.use_case: Reviewed as a teacher tool for differentiating lessons, scaffolding texts to reading levels, and generating background knowledge activities with cited sources.

identified_tools.name: Copilot
identified_tools.description: Microsoft's AI assistant for drafting, organizing, summarizing, and productivity support.
identified_tools.use_case: Reviewed as a teacher productivity tool for lesson-plan writing, classroom management, parent communication, and organizing student information.

identified_tools.name: Eduaide.AI
identified_tools.description: An AI-driven platform for teachers to create lesson plans, assessments, and instructional resources, including translation and feedback features.
identified_tools.use_case: Reviewed as a teacher platform for lesson planning, assessments, resources, and instant student feedback on writing.

identified_tools.name: Dreambox Learning
identified_tools.description: An adaptive learning platform that personalizes math and reading instruction and acts as a tutor for students.
identified_tools.use_case: Reviewed as an adaptive K-12 supplemental program that adjusts instruction based on student performance.

identified_tools.name: PowerBuddy
identified_tools.description: PowerSchool's AI-powered platform for personalized teaching, learning, and assessment support.
identified_tools.use_case: Reviewed as a platform for creating assessments, personalizing learning, and managing grades and reports.

identified_tools.name: Canva
identified_tools.description: A design platform with generative AI features for creating graphics, presentations, lessons, and posts.
identified_tools.use_case: Reviewed via its Magic Design feature for educational content creation and student projects.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a narrative review/article, not a primary evaluation study or meta-analysis. It summarizes tools and concerns but reports no original empirical outcomes for a specific intervention.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper provides practical descriptive guidance and examples, but no measured effect sizes or causal impact estimates. As a review, it is useful for tool identification and implementation considerations, not impact evidence.
